description: *Signal temporal logic* (STL) states properties of a trace, a sequence of time steps of real-valued signals, for example "speed stays at most 2 for the next 3 steps". Its quantitative semantics gives a *robustness* value `ρ`: positive when the trace satisfies the formula, negative when it violates it, and its size says by how much. Robustness is computed bottom-up: a predicate `x_i ≥ c` gives `x_i(t) − c`, negation flips the sign, conjunction and disjunction take the minimum and the maximum, and the bounded operators `G[a,b]` (always), `F[a,b]` (eventually) and `U[a,b]` (until) take minima and maxima over a time window that is clipped to the end of the trace. The crate uses `−ρ` as a cost to minimise, as a graded constraint violation `max(0, −ρ)`, as a *shield* that picks the candidate action whose rollout is most robust, and in `fit` to tune the thresholds of a template formula to demonstrations with CMA-ES. The evaluation is exact and takes `O(nodes · length · window)` steps.

papers.title: Robust Satisfaction of Temporal Logic over Real-Valued Signals
papers.venue: Formal Modeling and Analysis of Timed Systems (FORMATS 2010), LNCS
